These appeals and criminal revision coming on for admis  the court passed the following:
 ORDER

These appeals have been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 being aggrieved with the award passed by Ist Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hoshangabad in MACC Nos. 203/2017, 204/2017, 205/2017, 206/2017, 259/2017, 22/2018, 55/2018, 56/2018 and 57/2018 vide order dated 4th March, 2020 by which the consolidated petitions of the claimants were disposed of.

entities.text: Ist Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hoshangabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Along with above appeals one Civil Revision No. 37/2021 has also been filed under Section 115 of C.P.C.
2.

The facts giving rise to the claim petitions in nutshell are that on 4th February, 2016 deceased Brijmohan Pansari along with Vijay Nagar, Pawan Sen, Mahendra Sen, Jagdish Pansari, Vijay Pansari @ Gorelal, Radheshyam Pansari, Santosh Kumar Prajapati and Ashok Yadav were going to attend a marriage ceremony in Tavera vehicle bearing registration No. MP-04-BC-2731.
The driver of the Tavera Vehicle Vinod Prajapati was driving the vehicle with care and caution.

At 8:45 p.m.
The Oriental Insurance Com. Ltd. vs Smt. Sonu Pansari on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198491625/

sentences.text:
when they reached on the spot i.e. Budhni, Salkanpur road, the driver of the truck No.
MP-09-KC-9069 Jalam Singh driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner hit Tavera vehicle in which the claimants and deceased Brij Mohan Pansari were travelling.
Braj Mohan Pansari died on the spot and others got injured.
Claim petitions were filed by the injured and the legal representatives of deceased Brij Mohan Panari.
3. Respondents Jalam Singh, driver and Pramod Jaiswal, owner of the vehicle have not filed any reply and trial Court proceeded ex-parte against them.

4. The insurance company by filing the reply has denied the accident and involvement of the offending vehicle MP-09KC-9069 and further stated that the offending vehicle was driven by the driver without having any valid and effective driving license and the owner / insured was not having valid and effective permit and thereby, violated the provisions of Motor Vehicle Act.
Thus, insurance company is not liable to indemnify the injured as breach of conditions of policy.

5. The Claims Tribunal after recording the evidence of the parties and hearing their counsels have passed the impugned award by which claims petitions have been allowed and the liability has been fastened on the insurance company to indemnify the injuries sustained by the claimants.

6. The insurance company has challenged the award of the Claims Tribunal on the ground that insurance company has clearly proved that the offending vehicle on the date of incident was being operated without any valid and effective permit and on this behalf he has examined Mahesh Bhadoria (DW-1), employee of RTO, Indore and Sadaram Jhele (PW-11), Administrative Officerof the Oriental Insurance Company and R.K. Vishwakarma investigator.
All these witnesses have clearly established that on the date of incident the truck was being driven without any valid and effective permit.

7. Shri Rakesh Jain, learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company has submitted that the trial Court has considered but has ignored the effect of surrender of permit as provided in Rule 86 of M.P. Motor Vehicle Rules, 1994.
Thus, when the permit is surrendered, a fresh permit is required and if new permit is not obtained, it is clearly a violation of the terms of the policy.

By placing reliance on the judgments of Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Challa Bharathamma and others reported in (2004) 8 SCC 517, Rani and Others Vs. National Insurance Co.
Ltd. And Ors. reported in 2018 ACJ 2430 learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the insurance company be exonerated from paying the compensation amount.

Ms. Aparna Singh and Shri Sushil Giri Goswami, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents have submitted that the Trial Court has properly appreciated the evidence and clearly decided that the insurance company is liable and if in the situation that the insurance company is not liable to pay then the insurance company be directed to satisfy the award amount with the condition that it may recover the amount from the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.

9. On behalf of owner and driver learned counsel has submitted that it has brought on the record that the previous owner has deposited the permit before the RTO but Mahesh Bhadoria (DW-1) has The Oriental Insurance Com. Ltd. vs Smt. Sonu Pansari on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198491625/
7 not stated that permit was cancelled and no document was filed to prove that fact.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Claims Tribunal has rightly discussed the law and after that held the insurance company liable.
Hence, no interference is called for.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11.
In this case it is admitted that the accident has occurred on 04.02.2016 at 8:45 p, in Budhni Salkanpur road near Guddu Farms House.
Witness Mahesh Bhadoria (DW-1) in his deposition has stated that he was posted in the RTO office Indore in permit branch since 2006.
The permit was issued for the vehicle MP-09-KC-9069 in the S.No. 114/MS/CS/2011 from 08.03.2011 to 07.03.2016.
On 20.04.2015 the permit holder (owner of the vehicle) has deposited the permit in his office.

The vehicle owner Jalam Singh S/o Nagji Ram, R/o BijjuKhedi, Tehsil Saver, Distt. Indore on 0902.2016 applied for the permit and in response to that permit No. 795/2016/PPUC from 10.02.2016 to 09.02.2021 was issued for whole of the Madhya Pradesh.
12. He has further admitted that on the date of incident i.e. 04.02.2016 no valid and effective permit was issued from their office.
In this behalf he has issued letter Ex.D-2 signed by Amit Yadav, Junior Account Officer.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that from 08.03.2011 to 07.03.2016 valid and effective permit was issued but submitted that on 20.04.2015 that was surrendered before their office.

13. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that as per Rule 86 of M.P. Motor Vehicle Rules,
1994 if the holder of permit surrenders a permit for cancellation to Transport Authority which had granted the permit the Transport Authority shall forthwith cancel the permit so surrendered.
The permit was surrendered by permit holder Shri Pramod Jaiswal and on that basis the permit was cancelled.
In letter Ex.D-2 this fact has been clearly mentioned.

14. The opposite party as the owner of the vehicle has not produced any document to dispute this fact that he has not surrendered the permit or has not produced any document that on the date of incident 04.02.2016 he was having valid and effective permit, though he appeared before the Court and was represented by the counsel.

It is also to be considered that if the vehicle owner is relying that the previous permit was effective then why he has applied for new permit and on that basis the new permit was issued on 10.02.2016 as previous permit was effective from 08.03.2011 to 07.03.2016.

Thus from the above it is clear that on surrender of the permit, the RTO as per Rule 86 of M.P. Motor Vehicle Rules, 1994 has cancelled the permit and in that condition when the permit is cancelled, legally the vehicle cannot be plied on public road.
15.
The trial Court has misinterpreted the provisions and the insurance company proved that the permit was cancelled as it was surrendered by the owner.

In the judgment of Challa Bharathamma (supra) the Apex Court has held that when the vehicle is being operated without effective permit it is a clear breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

16. In the same way, in the judgment of Rani and Ors. (supra) it was held that when the vehicle was having permit to operate the vehicle in the State of Maharashtra and the vehicle was being plied in The Oriental Insurance Com. Ltd. vs Smt. Sonu Pansari on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198491625/
8 the State of Karnataka, is a clear breach of the policy and the insurance company may be exonerated from the liability.
17.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Com. Ltd. vs Smt. Sonu Pansari
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking to the facts and the legal position, it is clear that on the date of incident the owner and the driver was operating the truck without having any valid permit.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured.
18. As per the above cases, as cited by the appellant himself, in the case the injured are third party.

It would be appropriate for the insurer to satisfy the award and without filing a separate suit only by filing the execution proceedings, the insurance company shall be entitled to recover the amount paid by it from the owner.
19.

It is also made clear that before disbursing the amount to the claimants, the owner of the offending vehicle shall furnish security for the entire amount which the insurance company will pay to the claimants and if amount is not deposited within time, the Claims Tribunal shall be entitled to attach the vehicle as part of security.
If necessity arises, the executing Court may take assistance of Regional Transport Authority concerned.

20. With the above observations, the appeals filed by the insurance company and civil revision are partly allowed and insurance company is exonerated from the liability to pay the compensation amount but looking to the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Chall Bharathamma (supra)
and Rani and Ors. (supra), the insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount to the claimants of the claim cases before the Tribunal.
The insurance company is entitled to recover the deposited amount from the vehicle owner by filing the execution proceedings before the concerned Tribunal.
The Claims Tribunal, if required, is entitled to attach the offending vehicle and for that purpose the Claims Tribunal shall also be entitled to take assistance of the RTO concerned.
21. The parties shall bear their own costs.
22. With the copy of this order, the record of Claims Tribunal be returned back.
23. A copy of this order be kept in the connected cases.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE nks The Oriental Insurance Com. Ltd. vs Smt. Sonu Pansari on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198491625/

opennyai_summary.facts:
The driver of the Tavera Vehicle Vinod Prajapati was driving the vehicle with care and caution.
Braj Mohan Pansari died on the spot and others got injured.
Claim petitions were filed by the injured and the legal representatives of deceased Brij Mohan Panari.
4. The insurance company by filing the reply has denied the accident and involvement of the offending vehicle MP-09KC-9069 and further stated that the offending vehicle was driven by the driver without having any valid and effective driving license and the owner / insured was not having valid and effective permit and thereby, violated the provisions of Motor Vehicle Act.
Thus, insurance company is not liable to indemnify the injured as breach of conditions of policy.
5. The Claims Tribunal after recording the evidence of the parties and hearing their counsels have passed the impugned award by which claims petitions have been allowed and the liability has been fastened on the insurance company to indemnify the injuries sustained by the claimants.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
All these witnesses have clearly established that on the date of incident the truck was being driven without any valid and effective permit.
Thus, when the permit is surrendered, a fresh permit is required and if new permit is not obtained, it is clearly a violation of the terms of the policy.
By placing reliance on the judgments of Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Challa Bharathamma and others reported in (2004) 8 SCC 517, Rani and Others Vs. National Insurance Co.
Ltd. And Ors. reported in 2018 ACJ 2430 learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the insurance company be exonerated from paying the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus from the above it is clear that on surrender of the permit, the RTO as per Rule 86 of M.P. Motor Vehicle Rules, 1994 has cancelled the permit and in that condition when the permit is cancelled, legally the vehicle cannot be plied on public road.
15.
The trial Court has misinterpreted the provisions and the insurance company proved that the permit was cancelled as it was surrendered by the owner.
Looking to the facts and the legal position, it is clear that on the date of incident the owner and the driver was operating the truck without having any valid permit.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured.
It would be appropriate for the insurer to satisfy the award and without filing a separate suit only by filing the execution proceedings, the insurance company shall be entitled to recover the amount paid by it from the owner.
19.
opennyai_summary.decision:
If necessity arises, the executing Court may take assistance of Regional Transport Authority concerned.
20. With the above observations, the appeals filed by the insurance company and civil revision are partly allowed and insurance company is exonerated from the liability to pay the compensation amount but looking to the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Chall Bharathamma (supra)
and Rani and Ors. (supra), the insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount to the claimants of the claim cases before the Tribunal.
The insurance company is entitled to recover the deposited amount from the vehicle owner by filing the execution proceedings before the concerned Tribunal.
The Claims Tribunal, if required, is entitled to attach the offending vehicle and for that purpose the Claims Tribunal shall also be entitled to take assistance of the RTO concerned.
21. The parties shall bear their own costs.
22. With the copy of this order, the record of Claims Tribunal be returned back.
23. A copy of this order be kept in the connected cases.
